AND AWARD PASSED IN L.A.C.NO.05/2004 ANNEXURE-'C'.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR)
1.

In this petition, the petitioners seek the following reliefs:
"(a) Issue a writ, direction or order in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondents to pay the compensation as per the award passed on 16.10.2012 as per Annexure - F on 28(A) applications filed by the petitioners with requisite interest till date of payment, which is based on the Judgment and award passed in L.A.C.
No.05/2004 Annexure - C."
2.

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that in pursuance of the acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondents, the SLAO passed an award on NC: 2024:KHC-K:9364 30.09.1991,
which was enhanced at the instance of one of the land losers by the Reference Court in LAC No.5 of 2004 dated 23.06.2009.

Subsequently, the petitioners claimed parity by filing an application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which was allowed by the SLAO who passed an award in favor of the petitioners on 16.10.2012.

Meanwhile, in view of the Government Circular dated 13.09.2010 the award was sent for approval by the SLAO/Assistant Commissioner to the Deputy Commissioner, as a result of which, the petitioners did not get the benefit of the award and were not paid compensation.

The legality, validity and correctness of the aforesaid Circular dated 13.09.2010 was challenged before this Court in W.P. No.103554 of 2013 and connected matters,
which was allowed by this Court with a final order dated 11.09.2019 and confirmed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.A. No.55417 of 2013 and connected matters on 14.08.2014, despite which,
the petitioners still did not receive compensation.

Under these circumstances, petitioners approached this Court by initiating civil NC: 2024:KHC-K:9364 contempt proceedings in C.C.C.
No.200032 of 2021 which was disposed of by this Court vide final order dated 16.03.2021, which reads as under:
"The complainants, who have succeeded in their writ petitions in W.P.Nos.103554/2013 and 103691- 705/2013, have filed this complaint asserting that the respondents have deliberately violated the directions of in these petitions and as such they are guilty of contempt.

(ii) The action of respondent No.3 herein in forwarding the award passed by him under Section 28A of the Act to the Deputy Commissioner, the respondent No.2 for his approval is against the provisions of the Act, 1894.
Hence, the letter dated 16.10.2012, issued by the respondent No.3 to respondent No.2 at Annexure-E is quashed.
(iii) The award passed by respondent No.3 dated 16.10.2012 at Annexure-E1 is revived."

Smt. Archana P. Tiwari, learned Additional Government Advocate, who appears for the respondents, subject to the respondents' right to reply, seeks leave to point that the contempt proceedings would not lie because there is no direction in the writ petitions and the writ petitions are disposed of with a positive direction reviving earlier award dated 16.10.2012.

The complainants'
grievance is that despite the orders passed in the writ petitions, and the representation by them, the respondents have not revived the award, but this assertion cannot be a reason for initiation of contempt proceedings against respondents.
The earlier award dated 16.10.2012 stands revived by the directions of the court without any need for further intervention by the respondents.
If the complainants are aggrieved because some action pursuant to such revival is not taken, they will have to pursue appropriate remedy.
3. The submissions by the learned Additional Government Advocate will have to be accepted.

The writ petitions in W.P.Nos.103554/2013 and 103691-705/2013 are disposed of with a positive conclusion in favour of the complainants for revival of the earlier award dated 16.10.2012 without any directions to the respondents.

If the complainants are aggrieved because the action that should have been taken pursuant to such revival is not taken by the concerned, the complainants will have to avail the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9364 appropriate remedy in law but the contempt proceedings cannot be proceeded with.

Therefore, the contempt proceedings are dropped."
3.

The aforesaid contempt proceedings were closed based on the submission made by the learned Additional Government Advocate by noticing that there was no positive direction for revival of the earlier award passed by the respondents.

4. Subsequent to the aforesaid order passed by the Contempt Court, the petitioners submitted a representation at Annexures - K and L, both dated 06.09.2022, despite which, the petitioners have not been paid compensation awarded in their favour vide award dated 16.10.2012 and as such,
Shivasharnappa S/O Basavanappa And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84640394/
4
petitioners are before this Court by way of the present petition.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent Nos.5 and 6, and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1 to 4 did not dispute that there was NC: 2024:KHC-K:9364 earlier round of litigation between the parties and they are liable to make payment in favor of the petitioners in terms of the award at Annexure - F dated 16.10.2012, passed by the SLAO.
6.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and submissions made by both sides, I deem it just and appropriate to dispose of this petition, directing the concerned respondents to take necessary steps to give effect to and implement the award at Annexure - F dated 16.10.2012, and make payment of compensation in favor of the petitioners within a period of three months, from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
7. With the aforesaid observations, the writ petition stands disposed of.

Sd/-
